note: Report vocabulary, explained once at the end of a report and linked from each card. Keyed by term id.

group.label: Group patterns
group.sentence: A research association says that, across a group of people, a trait and a reading moved together on average. It is not a measurement of you, and it does not predict anything about you.

gene.label: Gene
gene.sentence: A gene is a stretch of DNA that carries the recipe for one protein. A change in the recipe can change the protein.

het.label: One altered copy
het.sentence: You carry two copies of most genes, one from each parent. One altered copy means the other copy is unchanged.

hom.label: Two altered copies
hom.sentence: Both copies of the gene carry the change.

dominant.label: Dominant condition
dominant.sentence: One altered copy is enough to raise the chance of the condition.

recessive.label: Recessive condition
recessive.sentence: Two altered copies are needed for the condition. One altered copy makes a carrier, who does not usually have the condition.

plp.label: Pathogenic / likely pathogenic
plp.sentence: A laboratory classification of the change itself. It says the change can cause the condition. It does not say the condition is present.

vus.label: Uncertain significance
vus.sentence: Laboratories do not yet know what this change does.

stars.label: Review stars
stars.sentence: ClinVar's 0 to 4 scale for how well laboratories agree. 2 stars means several laboratories agree with the same criteria. 4 means a practice guideline.

af.label: Allele frequency
af.sentence: How often a change appears among sampled chromosomes in a reference population. Rare does not mean harmful.

or.label: Odds ratio
or.sentence: How many times higher the odds of a trait were in people with the allele, compared with people without it, in one study.

beta.label: Effect size (beta)
beta.sentence: How much a measured trait moved, on average, per copy of the allele, in one study.

p.label: p-value
p.sentence: How unlikely the study result would be if there were no real association. Smaller is stronger. It says nothing about the size of the effect.

prediction.label: Prediction score
prediction.sentence: A computer model's estimate, not a laboratory classification. Models are wrong often enough that a prediction alone is not a result.

array.label: Genotyping array
array.sentence: A consumer test that reads a fixed set of positions. It misreads rare changes often, so a rare pathogenic call from an array needs a clinical test.

methylation.label: Methylation
methylation.sentence: A chemical mark on DNA that changes with age, tissue, exposure and disease. A reading is a value from 0 to 1 for one site.
